title: T1021.001 — Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated attack simulation: RDP lateral movement

steps.title: Scan the internet for open RDP ports
steps.caption: The attacker runs a port scanner against the company range. Port 3389 answers on one forgotten computer that was left open to the internet. This step creates no Windows logs yet, but a firewall or cloud flow log would show the scan.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Guess passwords against the RDP login
steps.caption: Now the attacker tries common passwords against a list of usernames. Each failed guess creates a Windows 4625 event on the target. The attacker keeps the speed low to stay under the account lockout rule.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Log in with the stolen password
steps.caption: A password worked. The attacker opens a normal RDP client and gets a full desktop on the target computer. Everything now runs inside a real Windows session, so the actions look almost like normal admin work.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Steal stronger passwords from memory
steps.caption: From inside the RDP session, the attacker runs a tool that reads the memory of lsass.exe - the Windows process that stores logon material. This gives them a domain admin password without touching the keyboard of any real user.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Jump to the file server over RDP
steps.caption: With a domain admin password, the attacker starts a new RDP session from the first computer to the file server. This is lateral movement: computer to computer, using only built-in tools and stolen passwords.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Copy sensitive files out
steps.caption: The attacker copies a finance folder across the network. The traffic uses normal file sharing, so it looks harmless to most network tools - but the volume, the time, and the account all break the normal pattern.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Delete the logs and vanish
steps.caption: Before leaving, the attacker clears the Windows Security log on both machines. This removes their story - but the act of clearing a log is itself a loud event that defenders should always alert on.
